## Quick and Flavorful Vegan Japanese Stir-Fry

This vibrant vegan Japanese stir-fry bursts with savory and sweet flavors, perfect for a speedy and wholesome weeknight dinner.

### Ingredients
- 200 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small carrot, julienned
- 1 bell pepper (red or yellow), sliced
- 100 g snap peas, trimmed
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce (or tamari for gluten-free)
- 1 tablespoon mirin
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
- Cooked steamed rice, to serve

### Instructions
1. Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
2. Add the cubed tofu and cook until golden and crispy on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove tofu and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the carrot, bell pepper, and snap peas. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender but still vibrant.
5. Return the tofu to the skillet and pour in the soy sauce and mirin. Toss everything together and cook for another 1-2 minutes so the flavors meld.
6. Remove from heat and sprinkle the sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds on top.
7. Serve hot over steamed rice.

Serves 2

*Fun Tip:* For an extra kick, drizzle a little Japanese chili oil (rayu) on top before serving. It adds a delightful spicy aroma!

Itadakimasu!
